children: Enterprise software and consulting company IBM

edged down 0.87% to $249.91 at 10:29 a.m. ET Friday, with its latest earnings putting cash allocation in focus. Software growth has momentum. The spending bill is hefty, too: acquisitions consumed $11.4 billion through September, compared with $7.8 billion in free cash flow. Friday's Motley Fool review revisited the software performance, but investors also have a balance sheet to weigh.

IBM's quarterly results showed software revenue of $7.8 billion, up 9% at constant currencies, while consulting grew 2% on the same basis. Free cash flow reached $3 billion, rising $700 million from a year earlier. That covered $1.6 billion in dividends roughly 1.9 times, leaving $1.4 billion before acquisitions and other financing demands. Total debt, including financing debt, stood at $63.8 billion. The business is generating more cash. Management still has competing uses for it.

The GuruFocus snapshot shows a GF Score of 76/100 and a price-to-earnings ratio of 21.31, with profitability stronger than financial strengtha useful reminder that earnings quality and balance-sheet capacity deserve separate scrutiny. The next test is execution: acquisitions need to contribute, consulting needs to build momentum, and stronger software sales need to keep converting into cash. Growth gets attention. Funding it well determines how much shareholders keep.

title: IBM Stocks Weigh Cash Allocation After Software Earnings Improve
